title: Boss: the log shipper ticket
summary: A ticket from the observability team: validate request ids, clean an email export, find slow requests and stop secrets leaking into the logs.

steps.title: Ticket OBS-207
body: > **OBS-207: log shipper fixes before the audit.** Assigned to you.
1. Request ids are `req-` plus 8 to 12 lowercase hex characters. Reject anything else at the edge.
2. The support team exports emails as HTML. They want plain text: drop every tag, keep the words.
3. Report requests that took at least a given number of milliseconds.
4. **Security finding:** API tokens appear in the logs as `token="..."`. Mask them, and do not lose the fields
Every part is about saying exactly how many, and stopping in the right place.

steps.title: Request ids
prompt: Match the whole string when it is a valid request id: `req-` followed by 8 to 12 lowercase hex characters
steps.explain: `{8,12}` sets both limits. Rejecting bad ids at the edge keeps junk (and injection attempts) out of every system downstream.

steps.title: Strip the tags
prompt: Each match is replaced with nothing. Write a pattern that matches one HTML tag at a time, so that
These exports come from one known template. Arbitrary HTML from the web needs an HTML parser, not a regex.
steps.explain: `<[^>]+>` cannot cross a `>`, so each tag is its own match. The greedy `<.+>` removes everything from the first `<` to the last `>`: the whole line.

steps.title: Slow requests
prompt: Write `List<int> SlowDurations(string log, int minMs)`. Durations appear as `dur=` followed by digits and `ms`,
for example `dur=1500ms`. Return every duration of at least `minMs` milliseconds, as numbers, in log order.
The number is the match without its first four and last two characters: `m.Value[4..^2]`.
template:
var dojoLog = "GET /a status=200 dur=12ms
GET /b status=503 dur=30012ms
GET /c status=200 dur=1500ms
GET /d status=200 dur=999ms
GET /e status=200 dur=ms";
Dojo.Eq("at least 1000 ms", new List<int> { 30012, 1500 }, SlowDurations(dojoLog, 1000));
Dojo.Eq("the limit is inclusive", new List<int> { 30012, 1500, 999 }, SlowDurations(dojoLog, 999));
Dojo.Eq("minMs 0 gives every duration", new List<int> { 12, 30012, 1500, 999 }, SlowDurations(dojoLog, 0));
Dojo.Eq("an empty log gives an empty list", new List<int>(), SlowDurations("", 0));

steps.title: Mask the tokens
prompt: Write `string MaskTokens(string line)` that replaces the value of every `token="..."` with `***`, and keeps
everything else exactly as it was:
A line may hold several tokens, or an empty one. Use `Regex.Replace`. Think about what a greedy quantifier would
do to the `ip` field. `System.Text.RegularExpressions` is already imported.
template: Dojo.Eq("the token is masked, the ip is kept", "user=\"alice\" token=\"***\" ip=\"10.0.0.7\"", MaskTokens("user=\"alice\" token=\"sk_9f8e7d\" ip=\"10.0.0.7\""));
Dojo.Eq("two tokens on one line", "token=\"***\" refresh token=\"***\" ok", MaskTokens("token=\"a1\" refresh token=\"b2\" ok"));
Dojo.Eq("an empty token is masked too", "token=\"***\" user=\"bob\"", MaskTokens("token=\"\" user=\"bob\""));
Dojo.Eq("a line without a token is unchanged", "user=\"carol\" level=info", MaskTokens("user=\"carol\" level=info"));
